takeaway: The robot works backwards from where the hand must go to an angle for every joint, and some places it simply cannot reach.

selfCheck.question: Why can't you just tell a robot arm "put your hand here"?
selfCheck.answer: the arm only controls how much each joint turns; something has to work backwards from where the hand should go to each joint's angle; sometimes impossible (outside the ring), sometimes more than one answer.

sentence: A robot arm can't move its hand to a spot directly. It can only turn its joints (base, shoulder, elbow, wrist), so to reach a cup it has to work out the right angle for every joint at the same time. Sometimes no set of angles works because the cup is too far or too close, and sometimes two different sets work (elbow up or elbow down).
